title: Timman Bagilla
description: Rice parboiled, then layered with broad beans and a great deal of dill and steamed under a cloth until a crust forms on the base. Turned out upside down so the crust is on top. Serves six alongside almost anything.
notes: Frozen broad beans are entirely fine here and save half an hour of podding. Slip them out of their grey skins if you have the patience — the colour of the finished platter is much better for it.

ingredients.name: turmeric
ingredients.note: for the colour of the crust

steps.text: Rinse the basmati rice until the water running off it is clear, then leave it to soak in lightly salted water.
steps.tip: Soaked grains lengthen instead of breaking, which is what gives the finished dish separate needles of rice rather than clumps.

steps.text: Bring the water to a hard boil with the salt, cardamom and bay leaf. Drain the rice and tip it in.
Boil for exactly seven minutes. A grain squashed between two fingers should still show a chalky line at its centre. Drain immediately.
steps.tip: This is the only timed part of the recipe that matters. Fully cooked rice here becomes porridge in the steam.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in the base of the pot, stir in the turmeric, and spread a third of the rice over it in an even layer.
Scatter over half the broad beans and half the dill, add another third of the rice, then the rest of the beans and dill, and finish with the last of the rice heaped into a low mound.
Wrap the lid in a tea towel, clamp it on, and steam over the lowest heat until the base has set into a crust you can hear when you tap the pot.
steps.tip: Do not lift the lid to check. Sitting the pot in a sink of cold water for a minute at the end releases the crust in one piece.

steps.text: Turn it out onto a platter so the crust lands on top, and break it up at the table.
